title: Accounting invariants and transaction processing
purpose: Find latent failures that produce incorrect transactions, balances, volumes, metadata, sequencing, or non-deterministic business state.
invariants: Every committed transaction must conserve each asset according to Ledger accounting semantics.
The same committed order sequence must produce identical business state on every replica.
Balances and volumes exposed by authoritative reads must correspond to committed transaction history.
Failed, skipped, or rolled-back execution must not leave partial business effects.
Preload, planning, and cache behavior must not change the semantic result of an order.
Numscript expansion and direct API commands expressing equivalent operations must preserve the same accounting invariants.
Metadata updates and transaction/account creation must be atomic at the command semantics promised to callers.
Integer/amount handling must not overflow, truncate, change sign, or silently cross asset boundaries.
adversarial_questions: Can a multi-posting or multi-asset transaction partially apply?
Can insufficient preload/coverage produce a result that differs from a fully loaded execution?
Can rollback or skip paths leave cache/state mutations behind?
Can Numscript generate an order sequence whose validation differs before and during apply?
Can metadata merges or account creation alter accounting state before a later failure?
Are zero, negative, extreme, or boundary amounts treated consistently everywhere?
Can transaction sequencing or id assignment diverge under retry or concurrent proposals?
Do balance/volume projections agree with recomputation from committed history?
